newsitem.title: FRANCE: French UNEDIC jobless fund expects 97 surplus drop.
newsitem.headline: French UNEDIC jobless fund expects 97 surplus drop.

text.p: The French unemployment benefit fund UNEDIC said on Wednesday it expected to end 1997 with a surplus of 996 million francs, well below the 10.3 billion surplus at the end of 1996.
"While the operating surplus in 1996 came in at 10.3 billion francs, the surplus could be reduced to around one billion in 1997," it said in a statement.
"In 1998, if reality lives up to a hypothesis of continued economic growth the unemployment insurance system would end up with a surplus of slightly more than 250 million," it said.

According the the "technical balance forecasts," revenue this year would reach 129.080 billion francs and spending 128.084 billion, meaning a surplus of 996 million. The cumulative surplus would reach 8.855 billion, it said.
UNEDIC expects the number or people claming unemployment benefit in 1997 to be 15,000 higher in 1997 than in 1996 but predicts that it could drop by 60,000 in 1998.
